rgraphtool (graph-tool-R) roadmap

Source: ROADMAP.md

Goal and scope

Build rgraphtool, a standalone native R/C++ port of the Python graph-tool library that can run R equivalents of the graph-tool cookbook, following its order from simpler to more advanced examples. Start with block models and the inference guide. Python is not a runtime dependency.

The target is graph-tool 3.9 from the official upstream, commit b24bc428e8426d0acb36b2d57bd61633335a3a26. The active adjacency headers come from this release. The flat SBM entropy and multilevel search are ports of the 3.9 inference headers (blockmodel/, loops/multilevel.hh, support/bisection_search.hh); reference values come from the conda-forge 3.9 build, run in the pixi environment under tools/reference/. Preserve upstream license notices and attribution when adapting code or distributing data.

R examples should express equivalent functionality, rather than copying Python syntax. Clearly document differences in indexing, mutable state, defaults, output formats, and supported graph types. The matplotlib and C++ extension chapters need R-native equivalents, not a Python compatibility layer.

User-facing API over callbacks: graph-tool relies heavily on user-supplied callback functions inside mcmc_equilibrate() to collect partitions, marginals, histograms, edge probabilities, and model-evidence traces. In graph-tool-R, prefer declarative function arguments and dedicated high-level workflows (such as sample_posterior(), collect = TRUE, history = TRUE, and future predict_edges() / reconstruct_network() helpers) so cookbook analyses run natively in C++ with ordinary arguments rather than mutable closure callbacks. Keep callback minimal—an optional power-user escape hatch, never the default path for core cookbook tasks.

Current state

All 14 roadmap milestones are complete.

Fixed-partition scores match graph-tool 3.9 to a relative tolerance of 1e-10 for directed and undirected multigraphs with loops, both degree priors, and groups whose degree sums exceed the exact integer-partition table (the Szekeres approximation is ported). Over 20 seeds on the football network, graph-tool 3.9 finds 1738.87-1747.64 nats (mean 1740.71) without degree correction and 1787.36-1794.09 (mean 1789.18) with it. The R port finds 1738.87-1746.92 (mean 1740.08) and 1787.36-1803.30 (mean 1789.89), in 0.004-0.03 s per fit. On a 3000-vertex, 15000-edge planted partition both reach the same optimum; the R port takes about 0.8 s against 0.8-1.7 s for graph-tool 3.9 on one thread (0.4-0.7 s with 10 OpenMP threads).

Nested scores match graph-tool 3.9 to within 2e-11 nats on 40 fitted football and 20 fitted C. elegans hierarchies, and on a 500-vertex multigraph with loops, directed and undirected. Over 20 football seeds graph-tool finds 1733.53-1738.32 nats (mean 1734.23) without degree correction and 1782.02-1787.55 (mean 1782.68) with it. The port finds 1733.53-1735.20 (mean 1733.94) and 1782.02-1782.37 (mean 1782.12), in 0.01-0.02 s per fit. Over 10 C. elegans seeds (directed), graph-tool finds 8459.65-8615.34 (mean 8506.34) and 8539.59-8662.94 (mean 8605.02). The port finds 8439.07-8578.20 (mean 8484.94) and 8515.98-8632.54 (mean 8573.18), in 0.16-0.22 s per fit (versus 0.22-0.33 s for single-threaded graph-tool 3.9). The sequential, lazily re-evaluated merges are a plausible reason for the port’s slightly better optima.

Milestones

1. First flat SBM example

Done when: the example runs end to end; fixed-partition scores agree with the pinned upstream reference within stated numerical tolerances; tests cover edge cases and compare inferred objective values without requiring identical stochastic labels or partitions. Complete. Direct group-level merge evaluation, flat hash maps (boost::unordered_flat_map), dense delta buffers, and integer lgamma/log tables bring single-threaded runtimes on par with or faster than single-threaded graph-tool 3.9.

2. Hierarchical partitions and refinement

Done when: the hierarchical cookbook examples run and refinement tests verify that zero-temperature accepted moves do not worsen the objective. Complete.

3. Model selection

Over 5 seeds on political blogs (1490 vertices, 19090 directed edges), graph-tool 3.9 finds 63037.5-63285.8 nats (mean 63148.4) without degree correction and 61347.5-61644.1 (mean 61469.2) with it (tools/reference/polblogs_nested_upstream.csv). The port finds 62980.2-63107.1 (mean 63043.4) and 61436.5-61558.8 (mean 61484.2), in about 1.3-1.7 s per fit (versus 1.5-3.2 s for single-threaded graph-tool 3.9). Both clearly prefer the degree-corrected model (() to (-1680); the cookbook reports (-1774)). On football both prefer the non-degree-corrected model by about 48.7 nats.

Done when: scores agree with the reference for identical states and the R examples report their comparisons without assuming stochastic fits are identical. Complete.

4. Posterior sampling

Exact small-graph checks on 3-vertex directed and undirected graphs verify that proposal probabilities normalize and match post-move reverse probabilities to machine precision (< 1e-12), and that flat single-node, flat merge-split, and nested 2-level merge-split MCMC reproduce exact Boltzmann stationary probabilities (both uniform at (= 0) and (e^{-}) at (= 1)). PartitionModeState and ModeClusterState description lengths, posterior_entropy, posterior_cdev, and flat/nested partition_overlap match graph-tool 3.9 to within 1e-10. On Les Misérables (77 vertices, 254 edges), flat equilibration and 500 thinned posterior samples (5,000 sweeps) plus mode clustering complete in ~1.5 s; nested sampling of 400 thinned hierarchies completes in ~0.8 s.

Done when: exact small-graph checks validate stationary probabilities or transition behavior, and seeded integration examples run with sampling uncertainty and convergence limitations documented. Complete.

5. Model class selection

Exact flat and nested overlapping description lengths match graph-tool 3.9 (OverlapBlockState and NestedBlockState(base_state=OverlapBlockState)) to within 4e-13 on complex directed and undirected graphs (with parallel edges, self-loops, isolated vertices, DC/NDC, distributed/uniform priors) as well as on Les Misérables; incremental half-edge moves match full recomputation to < 1e-13. mode_lprob(), cluster_lprob(), and nested/cluster mode_entropy() match graph-tool 3.9’s posterior_lprob() and posterior_entropy() to 1e-12. On Les Misérables (77 vertices, 254 edges), demo("model_class_selection") completes all 8 MAP model classes (3 restarts each) plus 6 posterior evidence integrations (200 thinned samples each) in ~5.6 s, illustrating how MAP favors flat/overlap (685.1–688.7 nats) while full Bayesian marginal evidence decisively selects the nested model (-log P(A) = 670.6 nats). Note that for overlapping states, posterior entropy in model_evidence() is estimated from vertex majority-group trajectories (a conservative lower bound on full half-edge posterior entropy).

Done when: overlapping and non-overlapping model classes agree with the reference for identical states, synthetic recovery tests select the true generative class, and the cookbook comparison workflow runs end to end. Complete.

6. Edge weights and covariates

Exact flat and nested weighted description lengths match graph-tool 3.9 (WeightedBlockState and NestedBlockState(base_state=WeightedBlockState)) to within 2.84e-14 across all 5 covariate types (microcanonical, empirical-Bayes, and custom-Bayes; DC and NDC; directed and undirected; simultaneous multi-covariate), and incremental vertex moves match full recomputation to < 2.84e-14. Single-node weighted MCMC is 1.2x–3.5x faster than single-threaded graph-tool 3.9 on lesmis and celegansneural (0.121 s vs 0.291 s for 500 discrete-geometric sweeps on celegansneural, and 0.010 s vs 0.035 s for 500 real-exponential sweeps on lesmis), and the full demo("weighted_sbm") workflow completes in ~1.4 s.

Done when: all five covariate models and nested weighted hierarchies agree with graph-tool 3.9 to machine precision, synthetic weight-only recovery and Jacobian-adjusted weight-model selection pass, and the cookbook example runs end to end. Complete.

7. Layered networks

Exact flat and nested layered description lengths match graph-tool 3.9 (LayeredBlockState and NestedBlockState(base_state=LayeredBlockState)) to within 2.84e-14 across all 16 reference configurations (directed and undirected, independent = FALSE and TRUE, DC and NDC, distributed and uniform degree priors, parallel edges within and across layers, self-loops, isolated vertices, and blocks absent from a layer) and to 9.10e-13 on 17-layer Les Misérables; 800 incremental vertex move checks match full recomputation to < 2.31e-14. Single-node layered MCMC is 2.5x–6.4x faster than single-threaded graph-tool 3.9 on lesmis and celegansneural (0.217 s vs 1.384 s for 500 independent = TRUE sweeps on celegansneural, and 0.017 s vs 0.067 s for 500 independent = FALSE sweeps on lesmis), and demo("layered_sbm") completes in ~3.3 s.

Done when: both layered model variants and nested hierarchies agree with graph-tool 3.9 to machine precision, synthetic layer-only community recovery and edge-covariate vs. independent-layers model selection pass, and the cookbook example runs end to end. Complete.

8. Assortative and ordered structures

  • 2020) in native C++ (src/planted_partition.cpp, pp_block_state(), pp_description_length(), pp_assortativity(), minimize_pp_blockmodel_dl(), compare_assortative_models()), supporting both non-uniform (uniform = FALSE) and uniform (uniform = TRUE) assortativity, DC and NDC, distributed and uniform degree priors, MCMC / posterior sampling / model_evidence(), and the Les Misérables assortative cookbook workflow (demo("assortative_sbm")).

Exact planted-partition description lengths match graph-tool 3.9 (PPBlockState) to within 1.07e-14 across all 16 reference configurations (directed and undirected, uniform = FALSE and TRUE, DC and NDC, distributed and uniform degree priors, parallel edges, self-loops, isolated vertices) and to 1.14e-13 on Les Misérables; 800 incremental vertex move checks match full recomputation to < 2.13e-14. Exact flat and nested ranked description lengths match graph-tool 3.9 (RankedBlockState and NestedBlockState(base_state=RankedBlockState)) to within 3.55e-14 across all 24 flat and 24 nested reference configurations (distance = FALSE/TRUE, unique = FALSE/TRUE, DC/NDC, tied and distinct ranks), with 1,200 incremental vertex-move and rank-relabel checks matching full recomputation to < 2.62e-14, and matching celegansneural flat and nested reference entropies to 0.0–1.82e-12. On lesmis, planted-partition MCMC (500 sweeps) is 4.0x faster than single-threaded graph-tool 3.9 (0.004 s vs 0.016 s); on celegansneural, planted-partition minimization is 22x faster with 174 nats lower DL (0.019 s vs 0.426 s), flat ranked MCMC (500 sweeps) is 2.2x faster (0.083 s vs 0.181 s), and nested ranked minimization finds a 78 nats deeper minimum (8583.9 vs 8662.2 nats) revealing an 8:1 feed-forward flow (54.0% upstream vs 6.9% downstream). demo("assortative_sbm") completes in ~0.9 s and demo("ordered_sbm") completes in ~6.6 s.

Done when: planted-partition and flat/nested ranked models agree with graph-tool 3.9 to machine precision, synthetic assortative/non-assortative and ordered/unordered model-selection tests pass, ranked layouts render cleanly, and both cookbook examples run end to end. Complete.

9. Large networks

Benchmarks on modular sparse multigraphs (<k> = 10): - 10-core Apple Silicon (macOS, 32 GB RAM): - N = 10,000, E = 49,794: flat default 3.88 s (1 thr) -> 0.905 s (8 thr, 4.3x, 2.8x faster than 10-thread graph-tool 3.9’s 2.54 s with 93 nats lower DL); flat strictly agglomerative (r = 0.5) 0.69 s (1 thr) -> 0.249 s (8 thr); nested default 7.62 s (1 thr) -> 1.85 s (8 thr, 11.1x faster than 10-thread graph-tool 3.9’s 20.60 s); nested simple_init 1.34 s (1 thr) -> 0.534 s (8 thr). - N = 50,000, E = 249,566: flat agglom 7.72 s (1 thr) -> 2.14 s (8 thr, 3.6x); nested simple_init 16.39 s (1 thr) -> 5.54 s (8 thr, 3.0x). - N = 100,000, E = 499,152: flat agglom 5.48 s (8 thr); nested simple_init 14.82 s (8 thr). Peak memory footprint holding both the 50k and 100k graphs plus LogQ(5000) (~100 MB) simultaneously: 604 MB. - Multi-core x86_64 Linux server (GCC 11.4, R 4.5.2, tested up to 64 threads): - N = 50,000, E = 249,566: flat agglom 14.53 s (1 thr) -> 6.43 s (4 thr) -> 3.46 s (16 thr, 4.2x) -> 3.11 s (32 thr) -> 2.99 s (64 thr, 4.9x); nested simple_init 31.16 s (1 thr) -> 13.78 s (4 thr) -> 8.51 s (16 thr, 3.7x). - N = 100,000, E = 499,152: flat agglom 32.38 s (1 thr) -> 9.78 s (16 thr) -> 7.90 s (64 thr, 4.1x); nested simple_init 71.23 s (1 thr) -> 26.70 s (16 thr) -> 22.94 s (64 thr, 3.1x). Peak RSS holding both 50k and 100k graphs and 64 thread scratch states: 791 MB. - Practical scaling & limits: 4–16 threads capture most of the parallel speedup (3x–4.3x) before sequential priority-queue merge commits dominate (Amdahl’s law), with incremental gains up to 32–64 threads at N >= 100,000. On memory-constrained machines, lowering options(rgraphtool.q_cache_max = 1000) trims ~96 MB from the partition-count cache.

Done when: portable multithreading, compact nested states, incremental NestedOverlap updates, strictly agglomerative search, and simple_init pass correctness and scaling benchmarks up to N = 100,000, E = 500,000, and demo("large_networks") runs end to end. Complete.

10. Uncertain network reconstruction

    • Measured networks with unknown Beta-prior or fixed homogeneous FN/FP error rates (measured_block_state(), measured_error_posterior()), matching MeasuredBlockState (Peixoto 2018).
    • Heterogeneous per-dyad Beta-Binomial error models with joint hyperparameter MCMC (mixed_measured_block_state()), matching MixedMeasuredBlockState (Peixoto 2018).
    • Extraneous edge probability estimates (uncertain_block_state()), matching UncertainBlockState (Peixoto 2018).
    • Latent Poisson multigraphs: fast \(O(V + E)\) EM (latent_multigraph()) and full Bayesian multigraph SBM (latent_multigraph_block_state()), matching latent_multigraph() and LatentMultigraphBlockState (Peixoto 2020).
    • Latent triadic closures (latent_closure_block_state(), closure_description_length(), infer_triadic_closure()), supporting \(L \ge 1\) generations of zero-inflated triadic closures over flat or nested SBM substrates and per-vertex \((t, m, c)\) transitivity statistics, matching LatentClosureBlockState (Peixoto 2022).

Exact description lengths, Beta error posteriors, conditional edge log-probabilities, and \(L = 2\) triadic-closure layer entropies and \((M, E)\) triad counts match pinned graph-tool 3.9 to < 2.4e-12 across flat and nested, directed and undirected, degree-corrected and non-degree-corrected configurations; incremental edge, vertex, and closure moves match full recomputation to < 3.2e-14, and the edge MCMC sampler reproduces the exact enumerated Boltzmann stationary distribution on small graphs to within Monte Carlo error (< 0.012). Note two deliberate mathematical fixes relative to graph-tool 3.9: (1) flat SBM edge deltas include exact edges_dl changes so incremental dS matches S(after) - S(before) identically, and (2) uncertain_block_state() uses the exact logit log(q_default) - log1p(-q_default) for q_default > 0 (fixing upstream’s log1p(+q_default) typo). Both cookbook demos run end to end offline in < 0.5 s (demo("uncertain_reconstruction") achieves repeated-trial ROC-AUC 0.99 with posterior error rates p = 0.196, q = 0.050 vs true 0.20, 0.05, and single-snapshot ROC-AUC 0.91 vs 0.84 raw; demo("triadic_closure") separates closure vs substrate edges with ROC-AUC 1.00).

Done when: all six uncertain/latent models agree with pinned graph-tool 3.9 to machine precision, incremental moves and exact small-graph Boltzmann stationary distributions pass, edge-prediction evaluation and triadic-closure recovery work end to end, and both cookbook demos run cleanly. Complete.

11. Reconstruction from dynamics and behavior

    • Ising equilibrium & Glauber dynamics (pseudo_ising_block_state(), ising_glauber_block_state(), including 3-state has_zero = TRUE) and continuous Ising (pseudo_cising_block_state(), cising_glauber_block_state()).
    • Compartmental epidemic cascades (epidemics_block_state(), supporting SI/SIS/SIR/SIRS and exposed = TRUE SEI/SEIR, plus dynamics_transmission_probs()).
    • Continuous Gaussian equilibrium & dynamics (pseudo_normal_block_state() with strict diagonal-dominance SPD projection and dynamics_precision_matrix(), normal_glauber_block_state(), and linear_normal_block_state()).
    • Generalized \(q\)-state Potts / categorical behavior (pseudo_potts_block_state(), potts_glauber_block_state()).
    • L1 (discretized Laplace) regularization (xl1, tl1), Gaussian weight priors (normal = TRUE), and Peixoto (2025 PRX) quantized MDL weight and node-parameter priors (xdist = TRUE, tdist = TRUE), plus declarative warm-started L1 regularization paths (reconstruct_l1_path()), greedy MAP
      • finite-temperature posterior MCMC (reconstruct_dynamics()), and native C++ forward simulators (simulate_ising(), simulate_epidemics(), simulate_normal_dynamics(), simulate_potts()).

Exact negative log-likelihoods across all 10 models and all prior components (geometric edge-count prior, conditioned and unconditioned L1/Laplace priors, and quantized MDL xdist/tdist priors) match pinned graph-tool 3.9 to < 1.2e-13 (note two intentional behavior improvements over 3.9: epidemics_block_state() fixes upstream’s unbound directed variable typo in EpidemicsBlockState.__init__, and Potts constructors do not silently mutate or rescale the user’s f interaction matrix). Incremental edge, node-parameter, and SBM moves match full recomputation to < 2.1e-13 across all 10 models. Both cookbook demos execute end to end offline: demo("dynamics_reconstruction") (7.0 s) achieves ROC-AUC = 1.000, F1 = 1.000 on equilibrium Ising (26/26), directed SIS epidemics (20/20, median t_hat = 0.450 vs true 0.45), directed LinearNormal (36/36), and \(q = 3\) PseudoPotts (26/26) while demonstrating how SBM+MDL eliminates pure L1’s bias-sparsity tradeoff (F1 = 1.000 vs 0.26–0.42); demo("empirical_dynamics") (0.31 s) reconstructs a strictly SPD partial correlation network on datasets::EuStockMarkets (1,859 trading days) and a 15-asset multi-sector Gaussian network (20/20 edges).

Done when: all 10 dynamical/behavioral models and L1/quantized priors agree with pinned graph-tool 3.9 to machine precision, synthetic and empirical reconstruction workflows and L1 regularization paths run end to end, and input preprocessing is documented. Complete.

12. Animation and interactive visualization

    • Native Hu (2005) / graph-tool SFDP force-directed layout (sfdp_layout()) with Barnes-Hut quadtree acceleration (\(N > 128\)), warm-starting (pos, max_iter = 1L), vertex pinning (pin), and inter-/intra-group forces (groups, gamma, mu).
    • Exact directed/undirected breadth-first search traversal and spanning-tree extraction (graph_bfs()).
    • Base-R graph rendering (plot_graph()) supporting vertex/edge visibility filtering, highlight halos, directed arrowheads, labels, and vector/raster R graphics devices.
    • Declarative SIRS epidemic animation (animate_sirs(), matching animation_sirs.py and animation_zombies.py via hide_recovered = TRUE, newly-infected halos, and fear_state = TRUE), dynamic spatial-segregation layout animation (animate_dynamic_layout(), matching animation_dancing.py with incremental SFDP + distance-shortening rewiring), and interactive BFS shortest-path tree explorer (interactive_bfs(), matching interactive_bst.py).
    • mode = "html" generates zero-dependency standalone HTML5 Canvas viewers that run headless during creation and interactively offline in any modern browser or RStudio Viewer (play/pause, frame scrubber, FPS control, live sparklines, and hover/click BFS inspection).
    • mode = "frames" exports numbered PNG frames via grDevices::png() (standard macOS/Windows/Cairo-enabled Linux R builds) for external video or GIF encoding.
    • mode = "device" and mode = "locator" require an interactive R graphics device (Quartz, X11, Windows, or RStudioGD); locator errors cleanly in non-interactive sessions.

graph_bfs() matches pinned graph-tool 3.9 shortest_distance(..., max_dist=3) identically across directed and undirected test graphs, and all 78 animation and layout unit tests verify determinism under set.seed(), empty/singleton/ self-loop/parallel-edge/disconnected handling, quadtree execution, HTML5/PNG output generation, and spatial-segregation edge-length contraction. All three cookbook demos complete offline in < 0.3 s combined (demo("animation_sirs") in 0.13 s, demo("animation_dynamic_layout") in 0.09 s with 25.7% mean edge-length contraction over 80 steps, and demo("interactive_bfs") in 0.04 s).

Done when: SFDP layout, BFS traversal, SIRS/fear epidemic animations, spatial-segregation dynamic layouts, and interactive BFS visualization work end to end offline with documented platform and display requirements. Complete.

13. Plotting integration

    • Property-to-size scaling (prop_to_size()), HCL colour mapping and standalone colorbars (map_colors(), plot_colorbar()), curved edges, vertex/edge z-ordering, axes/coordinate grids, and unified multi-format export (save_graph_plot(), using svglite when installed for SVG without XQuartz/Cairo dependencies and falling back to grDevices::svg()).
    • Embeddable base-R grid grobs (graph_grob()), tidy vertex/edge data frames (graph_to_data_frames()), and optional ggplot2 integration (ggplot_graph()).
    • Pure-R cartographic projections (project_coords(): Robinson, Mercator, equirectangular, Mollweide, and orthographic hemisphere clipping), spherical great-circle geodesic edges (great_circle_arc(), splitting cleanly across the antimeridian), built-in offline world coastlines (world_coastlines(), plus custom polygon support), and geographic network plotting (plot_graph_map()).

All 75 plotting-integration and map tests pass (0 failures, 0 warnings), verifying exact prop_to_size() scaling, Mollweide and orthographic projection geometry, trans-Pacific antimeridian great-circle splitting, grid grob and ggplot2 rendering, and binary file headers across PDF, SVG, EPS, PNG, JPEG, and TIFF outputs.

Done when: base-R multi-panel, grid, optional ggplot2, and geographic map-integration workflows run end to end offline across vector and raster formats without Python. Complete.

14. C++ extensions

    • Zero-copy graph extraction (rgraphtool::get_graph(SEXP) accepting either an rgraphtool_graph R object or its external pointer) and inspection helpers (num_vertices, num_edges, is_directed, source, target, edge_index, out_degree, in_degree, total_degree, checked_vertex).
    • Range-based graph iteration (vertices_range, edges_range, out_edges_range, in_edges_range, all_edges_range, out_neighbors_range, in_neighbors_range, all_neighbors_range).
    • Vertex and edge property maps (vertex_property_view, edge_property_view, make_vertex_property, make_edge_property) with per-access bounds-checked defaults (VertexPropertyMap<T>, EdgePropertyMap<T>, ConstEdgePropertyMap<T>) and upfront-validated zero-overhead unchecked views via .get_unchecked() (UncheckedVertexPropertyMap<T>, UncheckedEdgePropertyMap<T>, UncheckedConstEdgePropertyMap<T>).
    • Built-in kcore_decomposition() (exact \(O(N + E)\) Batagelj-Zaversnik algorithm matching pinned graph-tool 3.9 kcore_decomposition() identically on directed/undirected graphs, self-loops, parallel edges, and isolated vertices) and vertex_strength(), each supporting checked = TRUE/FALSE.
    • Extension discovery and compilation helpers (rgraphtool_include_dir(), rgraphtool_extension_example(), compile_cpp_extension()) plus bundled standalone .cpp examples (inst/examples/extensions/kcore_extension.cpp, inst/examples/extensions/weighted_degree_extension.cpp) and end-to-end demo (demo("cpp_extensions")).

All 34 C++ extension tests (tests/testthat/test-extensions.R) pass (0 failures, 0 warnings), including live compilation and execution of both bundled .cpp files and inline C++ code via compile_cpp_extension(), exact parity against pinned graph-tool 3.9 fixtures, and explicit verification of std::out_of_range bounds checks on checked views and upfront capacity checks on .get_unchecked(). demo("cpp_extensions") compiles and executes all three extensions offline in ~6.9 s, measuring 0.005 s unchecked vs. 0.013 s checked (2.6x faster) across 50 \(k\)-core passes on a 2,000-vertex, 9,996-edge weighted network.

Done when: the public inst/include/rgraphtool.h interface is documented and tested for graph iteration, property map access, and checked vs. unchecked access, and standalone C++ extension examples compile and run end to end. Complete.

Completion requirements for every milestone

  • Add runnable, documented R examples corresponding to the relevant cookbook sections, with data sources, attribution, and reproducible setup.
  • Verify numerical behavior against a pinned official graph-tool reference, using hand-checkable cases and regression fixtures as appropriate. Record deliberate differences and stochastic tolerances.
  • Test invalid inputs, graph direction, empty graphs, loops, and parallel edges where applicable; run the relevant package tests and R CMD check.
  • Specify runtime and memory limits, random-seed behavior, and platform-specific dependencies. Do not silently substitute a different statistical objective.
  • Mark a milestone complete only when its examples execute end to end; a partial API or scaffold is not cookbook parity.
